title: composed VeRA codes and Mirror views
hypothesis: Composing two per-factor Givens Mirror views recovers held-out combinations of a shared adapter family more compactly than VeRA-style additive scaling codes and an ordinary coefficient-product control; unrelated maps require private state.
physical_object: one frozen 12x12 core matrix plus a shared factorized adapter basis for the VeRA control
mirror_coordinate: one FP16 Givens angle per value of each of two task factors; compose left and right views
logical_multiplicity: 16 factor-pair maps, with 8 support pairs and 8 held-out pairs
controls: VeRA-style shared random rank-6 outer-product basis with sum of factor scaling codes

data.representation_fit_input: the eight exact full support matrices (post-fit screen); Mirror angle tables are the public teacher factor coordinates
data.evaluation_input: 128 held-out Gaussian inputs per factor-pair map; these inputs do not train or fit the codecs
data.aligned_teacher: W_ij = R(alpha_i) W_core R(beta_j), fixed angle schedule
data.unrelated_teacher: W_core plus independently sampled per-combination deltas

selection.tunable: none; all ranks, angle precision, codes, splits and seeds are fixed

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes after reload

success_gate: All 3 development worlds: held-out Mirror normalized MSE <=1e-5, payload <=50% of independent, and either >=10% fewer bytes than the best non-Mirror method at that quality or >=10x lower error for <=10% extra bytes.
failure_gate: Mirror misses held-out quality/storage or the VeRA additive/coefficient-product control matches it within 10% bytes; unrelated maps fail without evidence that factorized views recover them.

fresh.open_condition: only if the complete development Mirror-specific gate is met

boundaries: teacher shares the Mirror Givens composition chart
factor IDs are supplied; no router
zero optimizer updates; not capacity or natural-language evidence
